narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 65.9% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because the admissions process uses this prediction to assess risk, your application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your class ranking in your third year of law school was the strongest influence, pushing the model strongly toward predicting failure. Standing in the bottom decile is far below the average of accepted students (around the middle of the class), and the model sees this late-stage performance as a clear warning sign for bar exam success.

Your undergraduate GPA of 2.70 was the second most important factor. Although this pulled the prediction slightly in a more positive direction, it was not enough to offset the other signals. It remains well below the 3.23 average of students who were accepted.

Your first-year class ranking came in third. Like your third-year rank, being in the bottom decile here also pushed the model toward predicting failure, reinforcing the pattern of consistently lower performance relative to your peers.

Taken together, these academic indicators created a prediction that the admissions committee could not overlook. To improve your chances in the future, focus on strengthening your study habits and academic performance early, seek out targeted bar exam preparation resources, and consider reapplying once you have demonstrated clearer evidence of ability to succeed on the exam.
